args.notes: Source: blocks dataset (5760 rows, 5760 distinct blocks, no duplicates; no missing-value code; density and Cu have no missing entries, density range 2.30-2.90 t/m3, so density_table.txt was not needed). Density is in t/m3, Cu in percent. Break-even processing cut-off from block_value: 8 USD/t / (8500 USD/t Cu x 0.82 x 0.01) = 0.11478 % Cu; mining cost excluded from the processing cut-off (sunk once mined), as the tool does. Oxide (rock 1) and dyke (rock 4) treated as waste. Sulphide (rocks 2+3) blocks at or above the cut-off: 976 blocks, 2,628,068 t (tonnes = block volume x density, metric), tonnage-weighted mean 0.6962 % Cu, contained Cu 18,296.5 t in situ (before recovery). Cut-off value is quoted rounded to 4 d.p.; the grade-tonnage was computed at the exact 0.114778 value and matches. Not pit-constrained: the brief's 45 degree slope was not applied to this grade-tonnage question. For reference, a 45-degree ultimate pit on the same block values (pit45) contains 2,313,092 t of ore-class material and 4,616,548 t waste (strip 2.0); the pit-constrained sulphide ore tonnage is therefore lower than the model-wide figure. Undiscounted, no stockpiling. The client_terms document was not read as it is not needed for this calculation.
